blockers.quote: So what if a company could rent your brain while you slept?
blockers.why: Check #3 fails: the title question arrives, but the loss is not clear by 0:30; the draft says the cost lands around 0:55.
blockers.fix: Move this into the first narrator breath after the door, then add: “It pays by the hour. But every hour you sell is an hour your own brain doesn't get.” Cut the later duplicate at line 65.

blockers.quote: And you won't remember the work. Only small leftovers. The leaflet calls them crumbs: a taste, a word, a face that isn't yours.
blockers.why: Check #16 fails: the rule exceeds three spoken lines and never flags the limit that later solves the climax.
blockers.fix: Condense lines 88–100 to three rule lines, leaving line 94 unchanged. End with: “You won't remember the work. Except the crumbs: a taste, a word, a face that isn't yours. Remember that.”

blockers.quote: Eleven hours. So why not all day? You try. Noon, the bunk, the band on.
blockers.why: Check #20 fails: immediately after the city-wide hundred-window set piece, the story shrinks back to a smaller bedroom experiment.
blockers.fix: Move the all-day attempt directly after the bus nap, before the workplace, street and city reactions. Let the sequence expand bus → failed all-day exploit → workplace → street → entire city.

suggestions.quote: An eighteenth-century chess robot had a chess master hidden inside it (c17). Amazon named a website after it, Mechanical Turk, and paid people a few cents a task (c17). This is the human inside the machine. In bulk.
suggestions.fix: Compress to the value turn: “An eighteenth-century chess robot hid a chess master inside it. This warehouse hides a thousand people inside the machine.”

suggestions.quote: You'd rather sit in that chair every Thursday than build it every night.
suggestions.fix: Replace with “The company built its replacement out of your missing nights.” Then let the drawer action reveal the choice.

suggestions.quote: So, would you rent your nights? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
suggestions.fix: Ask the open question created by the twist: “So—which would you refuse to rent: your nights, or your days? Tell us in the comments.”

keep.quote: Sleep was never nothing. It was the one shift you always worked for yourself.
Sign, and nobody in this house sits in that chair again. Don't, and it's Thursday forever. You can't sleep on it. Sleeping is the job.
The biggest idea people ever had together, and nobody was awake for it.
